newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee rallies from early fall, forwards ease.
newsitem.headline: India rupee rallies from early fall, forwards ease.

text.p: The Indian rupee rallied in volatile trade to end Tuesday at 35.86/88 per dollar after touching an intra-day low of 35.95, dealers said.
The rupee traded at a low of 35.95 and a high of 35.85 per dollar on Tuesday, they said.
They said the rupee fell in the morning on dollar bidding by a state-run bank in eastern India but recovered as supplies of the U.S. currency came into the market later in the day.
"Some bidding by the state-run bank pushed the rupee down to a day's low of 35.95," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "But dollar supplies came in and the rupee rallied strongly."
The rupee recovered to 35.85 before some late demand from the state-run bank just before close of trade pushed it down again to 35.86/88, he said.
"Exporters seem to be holding out," said a dealer. "We will see good dollar supplies at levels above 35.95."
Dealers said premia on forward dollars ended Tuesday down from the day's opening levels.
"Forward premia went up a bit at the start of trade," said a dealer. "But the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was active in swaps, receiving forward premia. This pushed rates down."
He said the undertone for forward premia remained soft as domestic liquidity was good and the RBI was expected to contniue receiving till the end of the month.
The premia on six-month dollars ended Tuesday at an annualised 7.41 percent against Monday's close of 7.47 percent.
